title: Enterprise Audit Review, Analysis & Reporting
exclusions: This is the audit-record review/analysis/reporting control (NIST 800-53 AU-6, inherited by FedRAMP AU-6). It reviews and analyses already-collected audit records across actors and reports review-worthy activity. It does NOT cover whether records are being generated/collected (AU-2/AU-12 coverage — UC-22.35.6), the integrity/immutability of stored logs (UC-22.35.2), or automated response/containment. Service and machine accounts are scoped via the actor allowlist so routine automation does not dominate the review.
evidence: Saved search 'UC-22.14.82 — audit review, analysis & reporting' runs on the documented review cadence, writes each review-worthy actor record to the restricted audit_evidence index (7-year retention), and feeds the 'Audit review & reporting' dashboard — the timestamped operating evidence an assessor reads to confirm AU-6 review and reporting are actually happening.

compliance.assurance_rationale: AU-6 requires that the organization reviews and analyses audit records for indications of inappropriate or unusual activity and reports findings. This UC is the operating implementation of that obligation: on a fixed cadence it aggregates audit records across every actor and source, applies review heuristics (failed-action clusters, activity spikes via per-population z-score, high-volume actors), and emits a dated review record for follow-up and reporting. Splunk is the sole-sufficient detective control that performs and evidences the review/analysis/reporting cycle, so the grade is full; the human adjudication of a flagged item is the documented follow-up step, not a separate logging system.

compliance.assurance_rationale: FedRAMP baselines inherit NIST 800-53 AU-6 verbatim, requiring continuous review, analysis and reporting of audit records for in-scope cloud systems. This same scheduled control performs that review across the FedRAMP system boundary and produces the dated review evidence a 3PAO examines. Because the FedRAMP control text is the NIST AU-6 control, and Splunk is the sole-sufficient mechanism performing and evidencing the review, the grade is full.

compliance.assurance_rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM-03 requires that personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events. This control is precisely that monitoring function: on a fixed cadence it aggregates audit records per actor across all in-scope sources and flags adverse personnel activity (failed-action clusters, statistical activity spikes via per-population z-score, abnormal volume) into a dated review record. Splunk is the sole-sufficient detective control that performs and evidences personnel-activity monitoring, so the grade is full; human adjudication of a flagged actor is the documented follow-up, not a separate monitoring system.

compliance.assurance_rationale: The SOX ITGC log-review control expects that security and audit logs for financially-relevant systems are reviewed on a defined cadence with evidence the review occurred. This UC performs that automated review: it aggregates audit records per actor, applies review heuristics, and emits a dated review record retained in the audit_evidence index for the control owner and external auditor. Splunk is the sole-sufficient detective control performing and evidencing the ITGC log review, so the grade is full.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-22.14.82 positive (Enterprise, Audit, Review,, Analysis, Reporting): ingest synthetic events into `index=target_index` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `hosts`, `avg_events`, `sd_events` grouped by `entity` satisfies `failed_actions` > 50, `zscore` > 3, or `events` > 5000 for 'Enterprise Audit Review, Analysis & Reporting'.  Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-22.14.82 negative (& Reporting): ingest benign `target_index` / `target_sourcetype` events where `entity` stays below `failed_actions` > 50, `zscore` > 3, or `events` > 5000, or exclude the test entity via `compliance_exception_register.csv`. Variant 4 confirms zero alert rows for 'Enterprise Audit Review, Analysis & Reporting'.

dataSources: All in-scope audit/security indexes carrying an actor field (e.g. `WinEventLog:Security`, `linux_secure`, `aws:cloudtrail`, `o365:management:activity`, database and application audit logs). The optional actor allowlist lookup `audit_review_allowlist.csv` scopes out routine service/automation accounts. Collected via Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform (native). Splunk Enterprise Security optional for notable/risk routing of flagged actors. (Splunkbase) — Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742)
spl:
index=* sourcetype=* (action=* OR status=* OR signature=*) earliest=-7d
| stats count as events, count(eval(match(coalesce(action,status,signature),"(?i)fail|deny|denied|error"))) as failed_actions, dc(host) as hosts, values(sourcetype) as sourcetypes, latest(_time) as last_event by user
| where isnotnull(user) AND user!="" AND user!="-"
| eventstats avg(events) as avg_events, stdev(events) as sd_events
| eval zscore=round((events-avg_events)/(sd_events+1), 2)
| eval review_flag=case(failed_actions>50, "failed-action-cluster", zscore>3, "activity-spike", events>5000, "high-volume-actor", true(), "nominal")
| where review_flag!="nominal"
| eval reviewed_at=strftime(now(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
| table reviewed_at, user, events, failed_actions, hosts, sourcetypes, zscore, review_flag
| sort - events
description: Alerts on risk tied to Enterprise, Audit, Review,, Analysis, Reporting through UC-22.14.82 on `index=target_index` sourcetype `configured sourcetype`. Summarises `hosts`, `avg_events`, `sd_events` grouped by `entity` across `the scheduled window` before applying `failed_actions` > 50, `zscore` > 3, or `events` > 5000. Operators tune 'Enterprise Audit Review, Analysis & Reporting' using UC-22.14.82 runbook steps.
value: Tracking `hosts`, `avg_events`, `sd_events` via UC-22.14.82 on UC-22.14.82 search results improves response to 'Enterprise Audit Review, Analysis & Reporting' and reduces audit findings, regulatory gaps, and attestation delays.
implementation: (1) Confirm the in-scope audit sources carry a normalised actor field (FIELDALIAS to `user` where needed); (2) maintain audit_review_allowlist.csv for known service/automation accounts; (3) schedule to the documented review cadence (e.g. daily with a weekly reporting roll-up); (4) route flagged rows to the restricted audit_evidence index and email the review to the audit owner; (5) tune the failed-action, z-score and volume thresholds during a 30-day baseline. Indexes required: all in-scope audit indexes; Lookups: audit_review_allowlist.csv.
visualization: Table (user, events, failed_actions, zscore, review_flag) with flagged rows highlighted; single-value 'actors flagged for review'; time chart of flagged actors over the reporting period. Key fields: `user`, `review_flag`, `zscore`.

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AU-6 Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Authorised NIST 800 53 control testing** — Internal audit exercises 'Enterprise Audit Review, Analysis & Reporting' (UC-22.14.82) on `entity` during scheduled clause AU-6 sampling. Match compliance programme calendar.

2. **External assessor sampling** — QSA activity spikes `index=audit_evidence` `configured sourcetype` without crossing `failed_actions` > 50. Cross-check engagement letter in `nist_800_53_exception_register.csv`.

3. **Planned maintenance affecting control telemetry** — CAB change pauses ingestion to `audit_evidence` for `entity`. Compare `_time` with active change record.

4. **Third-party processor under contract** — BAA/DPA-covered vendor generates expected rows grouped by `entity` during normal service delivery.

**Suppression mechanism:** `nist_800_53_exception_register.csv` keyed on `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`, joined before alert threshold.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Enterprise ≥9.2 or Splunk Cloud. Splunk Enterprise Security optional (flagged actors become notables/risk).
• **Normalised actor field**: in-scope audit sources must expose a consistent `user` field — add `FIELDALIAS` in props.conf where a vendor uses a different key. AU-6 review is by actor, so this is the control's pivot.
• **Allowlist lookup**: `audit_review_allowlist.csv` (column `user`) lists routine service/automation accounts to annotate out of the review.
• **Evidence index**: provision the restricted `audit_evidence` index with retention meeting the strictest applicable obligation and role-based access for auditors.
• **Regulatory mapping**: this control evidences NIST 800-53 `AU-6` and FedRAMP `AU-6` (inherited). Every result carries `review_flag` and `reviewed_at` so the review evidence is directly readable.

## Step 1 — Confirm the review population

AU-6 reviews *all* audit records, so the base search deliberately spans `index=* sourcetype=*` filtered to events carrying an action/status/signature. Validate the population is what you expect: `| metadata type=sourcetypes index=*` and reconcile against the audit-source inventory used by UC-22.35.6 so the review and the coverage control agree on scope.

## Step 2 — Implement the search

The search aggregates per actor, then applies three review heuristics: a failed-action cluster (operational misuse / brute force), a per-population activity z-score (statistical outlier), and an absolute high-volume band. Use `eventstats` (not `stats` join) so the baseline is computed in-stream. Schedule it:

```ini
[UC-22.14.82: Enterprise Audit Review, Analysis & Reporting]
cron_schedule = 0 7 * * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -7d
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index
action.summary_index._name = audit_evidence
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.14.82,controls=AU-6;FedRAMP-AU-6
```

## Step 3 — Calibrate thresholds

Profile the population before alerting: run the aggregation without the final `where` over 30 days and set the z-score between p90 and p99 and the volume band above legitimate heavy users. Document the calibration date — an assessor will ask how the review thresholds were derived.

## Step 4 — Operationalize (dashboard + reporting)

Build 'Audit review & reporting': a single-value 'actors flagged for review', a flagged-actor table (user, events, failed_actions, zscore, review_flag), and a reporting trend of flagged actors per period. Enable scheduled PDF export on the reporting cadence and archive to audit_evidence — that export is the AU-6 reporting artdefact.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting and caveats

• **One account dominates every run:** it is almost certainly a service account — add it to audit_review_allowlist.csv.

• **No actor field on a source:** add the FIELDALIAS; a source with no actor cannot contribute to an actor-based review and should be flagged as a review gap.

• **Scope discipline:** reconcile the reviewed sourcetypes against the audit-source inventory periodically so the review population stays complete.

**Ecosystem integration:** Forward compliance detections to Splunk SOAR for automated incident triage and escalation playbooks. Enrich events with asset context from ServiceNow CMDB. Cross-reference with CrowdStrike Falcon or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint for host forensics and threat detection context. Integrate Okta or Azure AD identity context to determine if the acting user had appropriate authorisation. Feed validated findings into the GRC platform (e.g., RSA Archer, ServiceNow GRC, or AuditBoard) for regulatory compliance tracking and audit evidence management.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform (native). Splunk Enterprise Security optional for notable/risk routing of flagged actors. (Splunkbase) — Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`events, failed_actions, review_flag, zscore`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Every day we go through the records of who did what across all our systems, and we automatically pick out the people whose activity looks unusual — lots of failures or a sudden spike — so a person can take a closer look. We keep a dated note proving the review happened.
